what_happened: The operator deleted the scope-guard pause file for the replay line by hand. The file was written before rule a41d landed. That rule says attempts stopped by the environment no longer count as spend on the line. The pause is stored and never recomputed, so it stayed in force although all three stopped attempts on the line ended on environment causes. Removing it lets the guard re-evaluate the line under the new rule, and it will pause the line again if the signals still trip. The event lists no unmet criteria, findings or failed checks.
cause: A scope-guard pause is a stored fact, not a computed one. It is written once and carries no record of the rule version or the reason for the stop that produced it. When the counting rule was fixed, nothing re-ran existing pauses against it, so a pause made under the old rule stayed in force. This is the third operator lift on the same line. The fix to the rule did not reach the state the old rule had already written, and only an operator who notices can clear it.
prevention: Compute the pause instead of storing it. On each guard evaluation (and whenever the guard's rule changes), recompute the line's spend from the per-attempt stop reasons under the current rule, and clear or keep the pause on the result. If a pause file is kept, record the rule version and stop reasons in it, and have the guard discard any pause whose rule version is older than the current one and re-evaluate it. Add a test: a pause file written under the old rule for a line whose attempts all stopped on environment causes is cleared on the next evaluation.
proposed_request: Make the scope guard recompute line pauses under the current rule instead of trusting stored pause files. Outcome: when the guard's counting rule changes, or on any guard evaluation, a line paused under an older rule is re-evaluated from its recorded attempt stop reasons. Attempts that stopped for environment reasons (such as low disk) do not count as spend on the line. The pause is cleared if the line no longer trips the guard, and kept if it still does. Each pause records the rule version and the stop reasons that caused it, and the guard logs when it clears or keeps one. Acceptance: (1) a test with a pause file written under the old rule, for a line whose attempts all ended on environment causes, shows the pause cleared on the next evaluation with no operator action; (2) a test with a line that still trips under the current rule shows the pause kept; (3) a pause file with no rule version is treated as stale and re-evaluated; (4) no operator step is needed to lift pauses caused by environment stops.
